sources.title: pgvector README (Filtering section)
sources.quote: With approximate indexes, filtering is applied after the index is scanned. If a condition matches 10% of rows, with HNSW and the default hnsw.ef_search of 40, only 4 rows will match on average. ... Exact indexes work well for conditions that match a low percentage of rows. ... For more rows, enable iterative index scans ... If filtering by only a few distinct values, consider partial indexing. If filtering by many different values, consider partitioning.
sources.supports: Post-filtering on an approximate index returns fewer than requested rows for selective filters; exact search suits very selective filters; partitioning/partial indexes and iterative deeper scanning are the documented mitigations.

sources.title: Qdrant: Filterable HNSW (article)
sources.quote: This threshold is due to the decomposition of the graph into small connected components. ... A connection may be lost between two categories if they lie in different clusters.
sources.supports: Applying a restrictive filter during HNSW traversal can break graph connectivity and sharply reduce recall; engines add filter-aware graph construction/search (article describes a 2019 design, not Qdrant's full current behaviour).

sources.title: Sentence-Transformers: Retrieve & Re-Rank
sources.quote: Scoring thousands or millions of (query, document)-pairs would be rather slow. ... Hence, we use the retriever to create a set of e.g. 100 possible candidates which are then re-ranked by the Cross-Encoder.

sources.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT

sources.supports: Late-interaction models precompute document representations offline and avoid feeding each query-document pair through a full network; the abstract does not state the per-token storage trade-off or quality vs single-vector bi-encoders.
